faqs.q: Does my EMI change when interest rates change?
faqs.a: On a floating-rate loan, yes. Many lenders keep the EMI the same and change the tenure first, so ask yours how it handles rate changes. On a fixed-rate loan, the EMI stays the same.

faqs.q: Should I prepay my loan or invest the money?
faqs.a: If your loan rate is higher than the after-tax return you can reliably earn, prepaying usually comes out ahead. Home loan tax deductions under the old tax regime change the maths, so check your own situation or ask a financial adviser.

faqs.q: Will my bank charge me for prepaying?
faqs.a: RBI rules don't allow banks to charge foreclosure or prepayment penalties on floating-rate loans taken by individuals for non-business purposes. Fixed-rate loans can carry a charge, so read your loan agreement.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a flat rate and a reducing rate?
faqs.a: A flat rate charges interest on the full original amount for the whole tenure, so a 10% flat loan costs much more than a 10% reducing-balance loan. Always ask for the reducing-balance rate or APR before comparing offers.

faqs.q: Why is my bank's EMI slightly different from this?
faqs.a: Usually because of rounding, broken-period interest before the first EMI, or fees added to the loan amount.

sections.h2: How to use the EMI calculator

items: Enter the loan amount, meaning the amount you'll borrow, not the full property or car price.
Enter the annual interest rate from your sanction letter or the lender's website.
Choose the tenure in years or months.
Check the EMI, total interest and total payment, then open the schedule to see the month-by-month breakdown.
P is the loan amount.
r is the monthly interest rate: the annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100. At 8.5% a year, r = 0.007083.
n is the number of monthly instalments: 20 years is 240.

blocks.text: This is the reducing-balance method that Indian banks and NBFCs use. Each month you pay interest only on the principal still outstanding. Our guide on how EMI is calculated walks through the maths step by step.
These rates are only examples. The rate you're offered depends on your credit score, income, the lender and the type of loan.

sections.h2: Why your first EMIs are mostly interest

blocks.text: In the home loan example above, the first EMI of ₹21,696 is made up of ₹17,708 of interest and only ₹3,988 of principal. That's about 82% interest. The balance shifts slowly, and by the last few years most of each EMI goes towards the principal.
This is why a prepayment in the early years saves much more interest than the same prepayment near the end of the loan.

Paying ₹2,922 more each month saves about ₹7.76 lakh in interest. Before you pick the shorter tenure, check it fits your budget: many lenders want your total EMIs to stay within roughly 40–50% of your monthly take-home pay.
The rate matters too. At 9% instead of 8.5%, the EMI on the same loan goes up by ₹797 a month, and you pay about ₹1.91 lakh more over 20 years. Half a percent is worth negotiating.

faqs.q: How often do bank FDs compound in India?
faqs.a: Most banks compound fixed deposit interest quarterly. Check your bank's terms, because some FD options pay out the interest instead of adding it back.

faqs.q: What's the difference between compounding frequency and deposit frequency?
faqs.a: Compounding frequency is how often interest is added to your balance. Deposit frequency is how often you add your own money. They can be different, for example monthly deposits into an account that compounds quarterly.

faqs.q: Is this the same as a SIP calculator?
faqs.a: The maths is similar. A SIP calculator is set up for monthly mutual fund investments at an expected return, so use that one for SIPs.

faqs.q: Does compounding more often always earn more?
faqs.a: Yes, but the extra gets smaller. Monthly compounding beats yearly by a noticeable amount; daily beats monthly by very little.

sections.h2: How to use the compound interest calculator

items: Enter your starting amount.
Enter the annual interest rate and the number of years.
Choose the compounding frequency. Bank fixed deposits in India usually compound quarterly.
Add a regular monthly or yearly deposit if you plan to keep saving.
Read the final amount, the total you put in, the interest earned and the year-by-year table.
A is the final amount.
P is the starting amount.
r is the annual rate as a decimal (7% = 0.07).
n is how many times interest is added per year (4 for quarterly, 12 for monthly).
t is the number of years.

blocks.text: With regular deposits, each deposit compounds for a shorter time than the first one. The calculator adds them all up for you.

items: ₹1,00,000 at 7% for 10 years, compounded yearly, grows to ₹1,96,715. Compounded monthly, it grows to ₹2,00,966. Same rate, ₹4,251 more, just from compounding more often.
A fixed deposit of ₹5,00,000 at 7% for 5 years with quarterly compounding grows to about ₹7,07,389 before tax.

Saving ₹5,000 a month for 15 years at 12% a year, compounded monthly, grows to about ₹24.98 lakh. You put in ₹9 lakh; the rest is growth. The exact figure shifts slightly depending on whether you deposit at the start or end of each month.

blocks.text: Take ₹1 lakh at 7% for 10 years. Simple interest pays 7% of the original amount every year, so you end with ₹1,70,000. Compound interest, added yearly, gives ₹1,96,715. The gap keeps widening the longer the money stays invested.

Divide 72 by the annual rate to estimate how long your money takes to double. At 8% it's about 9 years; at 12% it's about 6. It's a quick estimate for comparing options in your head, not an exact figure.

sections.h2: Before you rely on the result

items: Interest on fixed deposits is taxed at your income tax slab, so what reaches your account is lower than the pre-tax figure.
Market-linked returns, like equity mutual funds, aren't guaranteed and change every year. The calculator assumes a steady rate.
Inflation reduces what your money can buy. At 6% inflation, ₹2 lakh in 10 years buys roughly what ₹1.12 lakh buys today.

faqs.q: What is a healthy BMI for Indian adults?
faqs.a: Indian guidelines treat 18.5 to 22.9 as normal. The global WHO range is 18.5 to 24.9. If you're between 23 and 24.9, it's worth discussing with your doctor, especially if diabetes or heart disease runs in your family.

faqs.q: Is BMI calculated differently for men and women?
faqs.a: No, the formula is the same for adults. At the same BMI, women usually carry more body fat than men, which is one reason BMI is only a starting point.

faqs.q: Can I use this calculator for my child?
faqs.a: No. Children and teenagers need BMI-for-age percentile charts, which your paediatrician can check.

faqs.q: My BMI says overweight, but I'm fit. Is it wrong?
faqs.a: It may be. If you carry a lot of muscle, BMI overestimates fat. Check your waist-to-height ratio or body fat percentage for a better picture.

faqs.q: How often should I check my BMI?
faqs.a: Once a month is plenty. Body weight moves up and down by a kilo or more from day to day, mostly from water and food.

sections.h2: How to use the BMI calculator

items: Choose metric (cm, kg) or imperial (feet and inches, pounds).
Enter your height and weight. Weigh yourself in the morning for the most consistent number.
Read your BMI, your category and the healthy weight range for your height.

blocks.text: BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)²
In pounds and inches: BMI = 703 × weight (lb) ÷ height (in)².

sections.h2: BMI categories: WHO and Asian Indian cut-offs

blocks.text: South Asians tend to carry more body fat, and develop diabetes and heart disease, at a lower BMI than Europeans. That's why a WHO expert group and an Indian consensus statement recommend lower cut-offs for Asian Indians.
It makes a real difference. The BMI of 24.2 in the example above counts as normal by the WHO table but overweight by the Asian Indian cut-offs.

items: It can't tell muscle from fat. People who lift weights often show as overweight while being lean.
It doesn't show where fat sits. Fat around the waist carries more health risk. A simple extra check: your waist should be less than half your height.
It isn't meant for children and teenagers. They need BMI-for-age charts that account for growth.
It isn't valid during pregnancy.
In older adults, muscle loss can hide extra body fat behind a normal-looking BMI.

mainEntity.name: What is a healthy BMI for Indian adults?

acceptedAnswer.text: Indian guidelines treat 18.5 to 22.9 as normal. The global WHO range is 18.5 to 24.9. If you're between 23 and 24.9, it's worth discussing with your doctor, especially if diabetes or heart disease runs in your family.

mainEntity.name: Is BMI calculated differently for men and women?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the formula is the same for adults. At the same BMI, women usually carry more body fat than men, which is one reason BMI is only a starting point.

mainEntity.name: Can I use this calculator for my child?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Children and teenagers need BMI-for-age percentile charts, which your paediatrician can check.

mainEntity.name: My BMI says overweight, but I'm fit. Is it wrong?

acceptedAnswer.text: It may be. If you carry a lot of muscle, BMI overestimates fat. Check your waist-to-height ratio or body fat percentage for a better picture.

mainEntity.name: How often should I check my BMI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once a month is plenty. Body weight moves up and down by a kilo or more from day to day, mostly from water and food.

faqs.q: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?
faqs.a: Start with your TDEE and subtract 250 to 500 calories a day. That usually gives steady loss you can keep up.

faqs.q: Why has my weight loss stopped?
faqs.a: As you get lighter, you burn fewer calories. Recalculate with your new weight, and check whether portion sizes or cooking oil have crept up.

faqs.q: Which BMR formula should I pick?
faqs.a: Mifflin-St Jeor is the default because it's the most accurate for most adults. Harris-Benedict is included if you want to compare.

faqs.q: Should I add calories burned during exercise?
faqs.a: No. Your activity level already accounts for regular exercise, so adding workout calories on top double counts them.

faqs.q: How much protein do I need?
faqs.a: It depends on your goal and activity. Use the macro calculator to split your calories into protein, carbs and fat.

blocks.text: It works in two steps. First it estimates your basal metabolic rate (BMR), the energy your body uses at complete rest, with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation. Then it multiplies that by an activity factor to get your total daily energy expenditure (TDEE).
Men: BMR = 10 × weight (kg) + 6.25 × height (cm) − 5 × age + 5
Women: BMR = 10 × weight (kg) + 6.25 × height (cm) − 5 × age − 161

head: Activity level
Multiply BMR by
What it looks like
rows: Desk job, little or no exercise

blocks.text: Most people overestimate how active they are. If you're unsure, pick the lower level.

items: Priya is 30, 160 cm tall, weighs 62 kg and is lightly active. Her BMR is 1,309 calories and her TDEE is about 1,800. Cutting 250 calories a day puts her at about 1,550; cutting 500 puts her at about 1,300.
Rahul is 35, 175 cm tall, weighs 80 kg and is moderately active. His BMR is about 1,724 calories and his TDEE is about 2,672. To lose weight he'd aim for about 2,170; to gain slowly, about 2,920.

head: Goal
Daily adjustment
Rough pace
rows: Up to about 1 kg a week; short term only
Slow, mostly lean gain with training
Faster gain, some of it fat

blocks.text: These weekly rates are rough. Your body adapts as you lose weight, so progress usually slows over time. The calculator never suggests less than 1,200 calories a day; going lower should only happen under a doctor's supervision.

sections.h2: Using the number with Indian meals

blocks.text: A calorie target only helps if you can estimate what's on your plate. Rough values for common foods, which vary with size and recipe:

items: One medium roti without ghee: about 100–120 calories.
One katori (about 150 g) of cooked rice: about 180–200 calories.
One katori of dal: about 120–150 calories.
One tablespoon of ghee or oil: about 110–120 calories.

blocks.text: Cooking fat is where most people lose track. Two extra spoons of oil in a sabzi add over 200 calories without changing how the dish looks.

For most healthy adults, Mifflin-St Jeor lands within about 10% of their measured BMR, but some people are further off. Treat the result as a starting point: eat to the target for two to three weeks, track your weight, and adjust by 100–200 calories if it isn't moving the way you expect.
This calculator isn't designed for pregnancy, breastfeeding, people under 18, or anyone managing a medical condition. Talk to a doctor or registered dietitian in those cases.

sources.title: Mifflin M.D. et al. (1990): A new predictive equation for resting energy expenditure, American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
Frankenfield D. et al. (2005): Comparison of predictive equations for resting metabolic rate, Journal of the American Dietetic Association

faqs.q: How do I calculate my age as on a specific date?
faqs.a: Change the second date from today to the cut-off date in your notification. The result shows your exact age on that day in years, months and days.

faqs.q: On my 18th birthday, am I 18 or 17?
faqs.a: You complete a year on your birthday, so on your 18th birthday you are exactly 18 years, 0 months and 0 days old.

faqs.q: Why does another website give a different number of days?
faqs.a: Usually one tool counts the end date and the other doesn't, or it uses an average month length. This calculator uses real calendar months and doesn't count the end date twice.

faqs.q: Can I find a date of birth from an age?
faqs.a: Yes. Use reverse mode: enter the age and the date it applies to, and the calculator works back to the date of birth.

faqs.q: Is my date of birth saved anywhere?
faqs.a: No. The calculation runs in your browser, and your date of birth isn't sent to our servers.

sections.h2: How to use the age calculator

items: Enter your date of birth.
Leave the second date as today, or change it to the date your form asks about, for example “age as on 1 January 2027”.
Add your time of birth if you want the answer down to hours and minutes.
Read your age in years, months and days, along with total days lived and the countdown to your next birthday.

sections.h2: Checking your age for exams and government jobs

blocks.text: Recruitment notices from UPSC, SSC, state PSCs and banks set age limits as on a fixed cut-off date, not as on the day you apply. Being even one day over the upper limit makes you ineligible, so a rough estimate isn't good enough.
Say you were born on 2 January 2000 and the cut-off date is 1 January 2027. The calculator shows 26 years, 11 months and 30 days. If the upper age limit is 27, you're eligible, by a single day.

Age relaxations for reserved categories, ex-servicemen and other groups are added on top of the upper limit. They vary by notification, so check the one you're applying for; the calculator only gives your actual age.

sections.h2: How your age is worked out

blocks.text: The calculator counts complete years first, then complete months, then the days left over. It uses real month lengths. If the day of the month hasn't arrived yet, it borrows the number of days in the previous month (28, 29, 30 or 31), exactly as you would on paper.
Here's a worked example for someone born on 25 March 1998, checking their age on 10 September 2026:

items: Days: 10 is smaller than 25, so borrow August's 31 days. 10 + 31 − 25 = 16 days.
Months: after borrowing, September becomes August. 8 − 3 = 5 months.
Years: 2026 − 1998 = 28 years.

blocks.text: Answer: 28 years, 5 months and 16 days, or 10,396 days in total. Shortcuts that divide total days by 365.25 get close, but they can be a day off around birthdays, which is exactly when it matters for a cut-off date.

In a non-leap year there's no 29 February, so the question is whether you complete another year on 28 February or 1 March. Countries and institutions don't all follow the same rule. For an Indian form, go with what the notification or issuing office says, and if it's silent, ask them in writing before you rely on it.

faqs.q: How do I count the days between two dates?
faqs.a: Enter both dates and the calculator gives you the total. Decide first whether the end date should count; it changes the answer by one day.

faqs.q: Does it account for leap years?
faqs.a: Yes. 29 February is counted whenever it falls between your two dates.

faqs.q: Can it exclude public holidays?
faqs.a: Not automatically, because holidays vary by state and employer. Use the weekday count and subtract your holidays.

faqs.q: How many weeks are there between two dates?
faqs.a: The result shows the gap in weeks and days as well as total days. 105 days, for example, is exactly 15 weeks.

faqs.a: Leave the start date as today and pick the end date. For a countdown to an event, the days until calculator is simpler.

sections.h2: How to use the date calculator

items: Pick the start date and the end date.
Tick “include end date” if the last day should count, for example for leave or a booking.
Read the total days, the same period in weeks, months and years, and the split between weekdays and weekends.

sections.h2: Should you include the end date?

blocks.text: This causes most of the confusion. From 1 March to 5 March is 4 days if you count the gap between the dates, and 5 days if you count both the first and last day.

items: Leave from 1 to 5 March covers 5 days, so include the end date.
A hotel stay from 1 to 5 March is 4 nights, so don't.
For notice periods, contracts and legal deadlines, check how the document defines the period before relying on either number.
From 11 September 2026 to 25 December 2026 is 105 days, exactly 15 weeks.
From 15 August 1995 to 11 September 2026 is 11,350 days.
90 days after 1 October 2026 is 30 December 2026.

blocks.text: The weekday count leaves out Saturdays and Sundays. It doesn't know about public holidays, which differ from state to state, or the second and fourth Saturdays when banks are closed. Subtract those yourself if they matter.

Months have 28 to 31 days, so there's no perfect answer to “one month after 31 January”. The calculator shows complete calendar months and then the days left over. That's why the years-months-days answer and the total days can look like they don't match, even though both are correct.
